chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I bequeath to the present one from my community, and the absentee, that he should answer the invitation of the Muslim, even if it is over five miles away, for that is from the Religion.'

key_terms.الشَّاهِدُ: the present one (one who is nearby)
key_terms.الْغَائِبُ: the absentee (one who is distant or away)

ai.seo_question: What is the religious ruling on answering a Muslim's invitation for a meal?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the communal obligation (fard kifaya or fard ayn depending on interpretation) of accepting invitations, framing it as a tangible expression of faith that strengthens social bonds. The inclusion of the 'absent' (gha'ib) alongside the 'present' (shahid) highlights the enduring relevance of this etiquette even for those not physically present at the time of the Prophet, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding the continuity of Sunnah. It serves as a practical guideline for maintaining Ummah cohesion through shared meals and hospitality.
